hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis, surgery, or treatment goes wrong at a Westlake Village-area medical facility, sorting out what happened can feel overwhelming. We can help you understand California's medical malpractice rules and explore your options.

about.title: Westlake Village Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Westlake Village residents rely on nearby clinics, surgical centers, and hospitals throughout Los Angeles County for care, and most visits go the way they should. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mishandles medication, the effects can follow a patient for years. California law recognizes that a poor medical outcome by itself isn't automatically malpractice — proving a claim typically requires showing the provider's care fell below an accepted standard, and a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in on that question. Because these cases involve tight legal deadlines and technical medical evidence, having an attorney who has handled this type of claim can make a real difference. We review the details of your situation and explain the realistic options, free of charge and with no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Pursue a Claim

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines Apply
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when the harm is discovered, and no more than three years from the date of the injury, to bring a claim. Missing this window can end a case before it starts.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Is Required First
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' written notice of an intended claim. We can help make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises
items.desc: California places a statutory limit on non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, and that cap increases each year. We can walk through how this may apply to your specific situation.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves uncertainty, so a poor result alone isn't proof of malpractice. A claim generally requires showing the provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, which is why an independent medical expert is almost always needed to evaluate the case.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in Westlake Village?
items.answer: California generally requires filing within one year of discovering the harm, and no later than three years from the date of the injury. Because Westlake Village patients often receive care from providers across Los Angeles County, it's worth having us confirm which timeline applies to your records and treatment history.

items.question: How do you handle medical malpractice cases?
items.answer: We review what happened and advise you on next steps, with no upfront cost and no fee unless there's a recovery.
